name: SUMIF
description: SUMIF adds up all numbers in a range that meet a specified condition. It's the go-to function for conditional summing — like totaling sales for a specific region or summing expenses above a threshold.
tldr: SUMIF adds values that match a condition. Give it a range to check, a condition to test, and a range of numbers to sum — it only adds the ones that pass the test.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: The range of cells to evaluate with the criteria. Each cell is tested against the condition.

parameters.name: criteria
parameters.description: The condition that determines which cells to sum. Can be a number, text, comparison (>100, "<>0"), or wildcard (*apples*).

parameters.name: sum_range
parameters.description: The actual cells to sum. If omitted, the 'range' itself is summed (must contain numbers).

basicExample.description: Sum all sales from the 'East' region
basicExample.explanation: Column A contains region names. The formula checks each cell for 'East' and sums the corresponding sales values from column B.

advancedExamples.title: Sum values greater than a threshold
advancedExamples.explanation: When sum_range is omitted, SUMIF sums the range itself. Only values >500 in B2:B100 are added.

advancedExamples.title: SUMIF with wildcard for partial match
advancedExamples.description: Sum sales for all products containing 'phone' in the name
advancedExamples.explanation: The asterisk wildcard matches any characters. '*phone*' catches 'Smartphone', 'Phone case', 'Cellphone accessories'.

advancedExamples.title: SUMIF with date criteria
advancedExamples.description: Sum transactions that occurred after a specific date
advancedExamples.explanation: Concatenate the comparison operator with a DATE function to create a date-based criteria.

howItWorks: SUMIF works in two phases. First, it scans the 'range' cell by cell, checking each against your criteria. For text criteria, it does an exact match (case-insensitive) unless you use wildcards. For number criteria with operators (>100, <=50), it evaluates the comparison. Second, for cells that pass the test, it takes the corresponding cell from 'sum_range' (or from 'range' itself if sum_range is omitted) and adds them all together.

howToSteps.name: Select the criteria range
howToSteps.text: Choose the column or range containing the values you want to test (e.g., the region column).

howToSteps.name: Define your criteria
howToSteps.text: Specify what to match — exact text like "East", a comparison like ">500", or a wildcard like "*phone*".

howToSteps.name: Select the sum range
howToSteps.text: Pick the column of numbers to add up. If omitted, the criteria range itself is summed.

howToSteps.name: Enter the formula
howToSteps.text: Type =SUMIF(criteria_range, condition, sum_range) and press Enter.

limitations: SUMIF handles only one condition. For multiple conditions (e.g., region='East' AND year=2024), use SUMIFS.
Text criteria are case-insensitive — 'east' and 'East' match the same cells.
SUMIF doesn't work well with 2D ranges — both range and sum_range should be 1D (single row or column).
Criteria must be a string, number, or cell reference — you can't pass a complex logical expression directly.

commonErrors.cause: sum_range is a different size than range — mismatched dimensions
commonErrors.fix: Make sure sum_range has the same number of rows/columns as range. If range is A2:A50, sum_range should be B2:B50 (not B1:B49).

commonErrors.cause: The sum_range contains numbers formatted as text, which SUMIF ignores
commonErrors.fix: Convert text numbers to actual numbers using VALUE() or reformatting the cells as Number.

commonErrors.cause: Trailing spaces or different formatting in the criteria range
commonErrors.fix: Use TRIM() to clean data, or use wildcards like "*East*" to handle minor differences.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: SUMIF works identically in Google Sheets with the same syntax and behavior.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Google Sheets also supports SUMIFS for multiple conditions. The behavior is the same as Excel.

faq.question: What's the difference between SUMIF and SUMIFS?
faq.answer: SUMIF handles one condition. SUMIFS handles multiple conditions and has a different argument order: =SUMIFS(sum_range, criteria_range1, criteria1, criteria_range2, criteria2, ...). The sum_range comes first in SUMIFS.

faq.question: Can SUMIF use cell references for criteria?
faq.answer: Yes. =SUMIF(A2:A50, D1, B2:B50) uses the value in cell D1 as the criteria. Combine with operators: =SUMIF(A2:A50, ">"&D1, B2:B50).

faq.question: Why does SUMIF return 0?
faq.answer: Common causes: (1) numbers stored as text in sum_range, (2) mismatched range sizes, (3) criteria not matching any cells. Check data formatting first.

faq.question: Can SUMIF sum based on color?
faq.answer: No. SUMIF cannot filter by cell color or font color. You'd need a VBA macro or manual filtering for color-based summing.

faq.question: How do I sum with two conditions?
faq.answer: Use SUMIFS instead: =SUMIFS(B2:B50, A2:A50, "East", C2:C50, "2024") sums column B where A is 'East' AND C is '2024'.
